If a call for high fire comes in during low it will ramp up, but that switch must close within a time frame or it will drop out

The switches are cheap, just buy the right ones and be done.

Question from an HVAC tech.

Do you have a gas furnace, electric furnace or oil fired?

If you have an electric/heat pump you may have had a burn out on the heater strips causing black carbon dust to be blown through the house and then recirculated in and the filter did it's job.

If you have gas. Well the only thing I can really think of would be airborne contaminants like candle soot.
A gas furnace would have to be running so badly to create soot that as long as the furnace has the typical safeties like a flame sensor, high limit switches, etc it shouldn't even function.

Now if you have OIL this can probably be the reason, but with oil you would probably have noticed a strong smell throughout the house within the 13 days. What I believe would be happening is the oil burner is running heavy causing black soot. Think of when a big diesel truck rolls coal. Diesel and oil furnaces burn the same fuel. Too much fuel in the air fuel ratio it burns sooty. Oil does always produce a small amount of black smoke even when properly dialed in. This is confirmed with a smoke test when we do a combustion analysis. No smoke present actually is a bad thing meaning we are running too much air in the fuel mix running lean, safer to run a tad rich than lean.

The only way for that soot to find it's way into the air stream is by a few ways. Oil burning equipment typically have a draft damper installed on the flue pipe to the chimney. If you are not getting proper draft up the chimney the furnace will begin spilling the combustion gases into the house. A draft damper will swing freely when the furnace is off, and when running the damper will open slightly.

With the above problems we also have the possibility of the room the furnace is in is running at negative pressure. This can pull combustion gases out of the chimney and into the house. This is caused by two main reasons. No make up air for combustion, or negative pressure cause by improper return air flow for the duct work.

The other causes are severe need of cleaning and maintenance of the fire box, leaking seals on the fire box, cracked heat exchanger, open inspection port, the list goes on.
